subject: chemistry
title: Concentration in mol/dm³
key_idea: (Higher tier, separate chemistry) Concentration can also be measured in mol/dm³, the number of moles of solute in 1 dm³ of solution. Use it to find the moles in any volume, and multiply by Mr to convert between mol/dm³ and g/dm³.

blocks.text: (Higher tier, separate chemistry) Chemists often give a concentration in moles, not grams. This section covers what mol/dm³ means and how to use it.

items.meaning: The number of moles of solute in 1 dm³ (1000 cm³) of solution.

blocks.label: Concentration
blocks.formula: concentration (mol/dm³) = moles of solute ÷ volume of solution (dm³)
where: volume in dm³: divide cm³ by 1000

items.text: 25.0 cm³ of 0.124 mol/dm³ sodium carbonate. 25.0 ÷ 1000 = 0.0250 dm³.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the moles of solute from a concentration and a volume in cm³.
diagram.question: Calculate the number of moles of solute in **{V} cm³** of a solution with a concentration of **{c} mol/dm³**.

items: Divide cm³ by 1000 to get dm³.

blocks.text: (Higher tier, separate chemistry) The relative formula mass links grams to moles. Use it to change one unit of concentration into the other.

blocks.label: mol/dm³ to g/dm³
blocks.formula: concentration in g/dm³ = concentration in mol/dm³ × Mr
where: Mr = relative formula mass of the solute

blocks.label: g/dm³ to mol/dm³
blocks.formula: concentration in mol/dm³ = concentration in g/dm³ ÷ Mr

items.text: Sulfuric acid is 0.250 mol/dm³. Mr of H₂SO₄ = 98. 0.250 × 98 = 24.5 g/dm³.
Copper sulfate is 15.95 g/dm³. Mr of CuSO₄ = 63.5 + 32 + (4 × 16) = 159.5. 15.95 ÷ 159.5 = 0.1 mol/dm³.

diagram.alt: Practise converting a concentration in mol/dm³ to g/dm³ for sodium hydroxide.
diagram.question: A sodium hydroxide solution has a concentration of **{c} mol/dm³**. Calculate its concentration in g/dm³. (Ar: Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)

blocks.text: If the volumes of two solutions that react completely are known, and the concentration of one is known, the concentration of the other can be found. That is a titration calculation.

items: Find Mr from the formula first.

checks.q: State what a concentration of 0.5 mol/dm³ means.
checks.a: There is 0.5 mol of solute in every 1 dm³ of solution.

checks.q: Calculate the moles of NaOH in 25.0 cm³ of a 0.200 mol/dm³ solution.

worked_example.question:
25.00 cm³ of hydrochloric acid reacted with 23.50 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ barium hydroxide solution.

The equation for the reaction is:

2HCl(aq) + Ba(OH)₂(aq) → BaCl₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l)

Calculate the concentration of the hydrochloric acid in mol/dm³.
worked_example.tip: Marks follow your own working if an earlier step is wrong, so show each step.

worked_example.question:
Pieces of zinc react with copper sulfate solution.

Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)

The copper sulfate solution used has a concentration of 15.95 g dm⁻³.

Calculate the number of moles of copper sulfate, CuSO₄, in 50.00 cm³ of this solution.

(relative atomic masses: O = 16, S = 32, Cu = 63.5)
worked_example.tip: Or convert first: concentration = 15.95 ÷ 159.5 = 0.1 mol dm⁻³, then moles = 50 ÷ 1000 × 0.1 = 0.005.

worked_example.question:
A student dissolves 0.6 g of zinc sulfate in 250 cm³ of water.

The volume of the water is 0.25 dm³.

Use this volume to calculate the concentration of the zinc sulfate in g/dm³.
worked_example.tip: The volume must be in dm³. 250 cm³ ÷ 1000 = 0.25 dm³. To change g/dm³ into mol/dm³, divide by the Mr.

worked_example.question:
A student needs 21.50 cm³ of hydrochloric acid to neutralise 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.800 mol/dm³.

The equation for the reaction is

NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

Calculate the concentration, in mol/dm³, of the hydrochloric acid.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the moles, one for dividing by the volume in dm³ and one for the answer.
